Food · Designs for testing

Hunger, designed.

Chicken 65 from South India, rethought for masa totopos. A braise that borrows from two kitchens. A wider set of dishes is specified; five core dishes are the first to be tested in a home kitchen. None are cooked for guests. None are for sale.

NASHA is in development. There is no brewery, no restaurant, no truck and no menu for sale yet. Images are concept visualizations and illustrations, not photographs of NASHA. The drawings are proposed presentation, not our finished dishes.

Chicken 65 Totopos

IN DEVELOPMENT Not cooked

Bite-sized fried boneless chicken thigh in the style of South Indian Chicken 65, served on and with thick fried corn chips. It is a design in development and has not been cooked.

Why it exists. The chip becomes the plate, so chicken and chip are built to be eaten together. It is a shareable, hands-on opener that shows the Indo-Mex idea immediately.

The full design
Indian component
Chicken 65 with a yogurt, ginger, garlic and lemon marinade, curry leaf and green chile. It is associated with Chennai, but its origin is contested.
Mexican component
Fried nixtamal corn totopos as the base, with lime, onion and crema. The thick chip is NASHA's own design choice, not a Mexican standard.
Fusion logic
The chicken and chip are eaten as one bite, with crema as an optional cooler in place of raita. Three constructions (integrated, ring, composed board) are planned for comparison.
Texture target
Crisp-shell juicy chicken; chip still crisp at T+10 (gate 3.5)
Heat
medium (green chile, red chilli)
Acid
lemon in marinade, lime at service
Portion
Shareable board or plate; exact amounts are still to be set in testing.
Plating
Board or plate, with crema on the side or worked in depending on the construction under test.
Cannot change without losing the dish
Boneless chicken thigh, rice flour and cornflour coating, curry leaf, green chile, fried corn tortilla wedges, lime.
Beer idea
Mexican-Style Lager (alternate: Pilsner)
Zero-proof idea
An agua-fresca-style drink of fruit, lime and a little salt: bright, acidic and lightly savory, served very cold.
Operating risk
HIGH: moisture migration into chip; 10-minute failure gate
Cultural care
Medium. The Chicken 65 origin and the Hyderabad or Andhra lineage are unconfirmed, so no single origin story should be told, and an advisor should review.
Next test
Session 1 exactly as frozen (sheet 13 shopping list and cook card)

Paneer Tikka Taco

IN DEVELOPMENT Not cooked

A small corn-tortilla taco filled with charred, spiced paneer, green salsa, raw onion, cilantro and lime. It has not been cooked.

Why it exists. It gives vegetarian guests a hero dish rather than a side, and shows that tikka char and taco freshness fit naturally together.

The full design
Indian component
Paneer tikka: a thick hung-curd marinade, char and soft paneer. It comes from the North Indian and Punjabi restaurant tradition, and no inventor is documented.
Mexican component
Corn tortilla with salsa verde, onion, cilantro and lime; the taco form is Mexican-inspired. Optional charred pineapple is an echo of al pastor but is never called that.
Fusion logic
Tandoor-style char on a taco, with salsa and lime doing the job that raita and chutney do beside tikka.
Texture target
Soft interior, visible char, crust that clings; tortilla does not tear
Heat
medium
Acid
lime, salsa verde, pickled red onion
Portion
Two small tacos per order.
Plating
Two tacos on a plate with salsa on the side.
Cannot change without losing the dish
Paneer, hung-curd marinade with ginger, garlic, chile, kasuri methi and chaat masala, corn tortilla, salsa verde, onion, cilantro, lime.
Beer idea
Witbier (alternate: Mexican-Style Lager)
Zero-proof idea
A spiced-citrus drink with a gentle herbal edge and light sparkle that echoes lime and cilantro.
Operating risk
MEDIUM-HIGH: paneer firms and dries, tortilla steams; finish to order
Cultural care
Medium. Pineapple is flagged as uncertain and needs advisor input, and the taco form and tikka are both borrowed, so both cultures should be credited plainly.
Next test
Session 2: ONE variable = heat source; marinade, cut, tortilla constant; hold at 0/5/10 min

Goat Birria, Sealed-Pot Braise

IN DEVELOPMENT Not cooked

A slow braise of bone-in goat in a guajillo and ancho chile adobo, served as tacos with a small cup of consomme. It has not been cooked and is a long-lead item.

Why it exists. Birria de chivo is a Jalisco dish whose original meat is goat, and it lets NASHA make a rich, deep centrepiece that clearly reads as goat.

The full design
Indian component
Technique only: dum-style sealed-pot braising, whole-spice toasting and bhuna-style frying of the adobo paste. Yogurt-papaya and curry-leaf ideas are tested against a plain adobo, not assumed.
Mexican component
Goat, chile adobo, consomme, corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime and salsa. These are historically supported from web sources, with a Mexican advisor still to confirm.
Fusion logic
The Mexican dish stays whole, and the Indian layer is included only where tasting shows it adds depth. The dipped and griddled taco form is a modern adaptation.
Texture target
Tender but fibrous goat; drinkable consomme; tortilla holds after dipping
Heat
medium
Acid
vinegar in adobo, lime, salsa
Portion
Taco or tacos with consomme in a small cup; no cheese by default.
Plating
Tacos on a plate and consomme in a small clay or steel cup, with bones and fibre kept visible.
Cannot change without losing the dish
Bone-in goat, guajillo and ancho adobo, goat, chicken or vegetable stock only, corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime.
Beer idea
Hefeweizen (alternate: Vienna Amber)
Zero-proof idea
A tea-based drink with tamarind or hibiscus acid and warm spice, served cool or slightly warm, matching the dish's chile and cinnamon notes.
Operating risk
HIGH: large braise cooling/reheating/hold, fat set in consomme (food-safety professional must set the process)
Cultural care
Higher. Birria is a living Mexican regional dish, so Mexican advisor review is needed, and the sealed-pot link to India is a parallel rather than a shared origin.
Next test
Small pilot per the Session 5 card (about 3 kg bone-in): plain adobo vs adobo+Indian layer (one variable), record yield, trim, skim, 60/120 min hold; blind vs lamb taco

Gobi Taco

IN DEVELOPMENT Not cooked

A corn-tortilla taco with roasted cauliflower florets, a tamarind and guajillo glaze, lime slaw, salsa, pickled onion and cilantro. It has not been cooked.

Why it exists. It is a vegetarian taco meant to stand on its own, with the cauliflower recognisable and not hidden under batter.

The full design
Indian component
Inspired by Gobi 65 and tandoori gobi. Gobi Manchurian is Indo-Chinese and is only named if actually used.
Mexican component
Corn tortilla, lime-cabbage slaw, salsa, pickled onion and cilantro. No traditional Mexican cauliflower taco is claimed.
Fusion logic
Roast-first cauliflower with a late tamarind and guajillo glaze, so slaw and pickle add the acid and crunch. A batter-fried version is a comparison, and fry versus roast is still undecided.
Texture target
Visible florets with dark tips and cream stems; crunch retained 10 min
Heat
medium
Acid
tamarind, lime slaw, pickled onion
Portion
Two tacos, three to four florets per taco.
Plating
Two tacos, with salsa on the side and slaw and glaze added at the last moment.
Cannot change without losing the dish
Cauliflower florets, tamarind and guajillo glaze, lime slaw, corn tortilla, pickled onion, cilantro.
Beer idea
Pilsner (alternate: Mexican-Style Lager)
Zero-proof idea
A lime-forward agua-fresca-style drink with a pinch of salt and a little green herb, cold and crisp.
Operating risk
MEDIUM-HIGH: cauliflower keeps releasing water; glaze and slaw soften crust
Cultural care
Lower to medium. The glaze is an original house idea with no claimed precedent, and the dish should be called modern fusion and not traditional.
Next test
Write a Gobi Taco test sheet first; primary question fry vs roast; crunch at 0/5/10/15 min; glaze grams vs tortilla softening

Butter Chicken & Roasted Poblano Quesadilla

IN DEVELOPMENT Not cooked

A griddled quesadilla filled with reduced butter chicken, charred chicken, melting cheese and roasted poblano strips. It has not been cooked.

Why it exists. It takes one of the best-known Indian comfort dishes and puts it in a handheld, shareable Mexican form.

The full design
Indian component
Murgh makhani: a tomato, butter and cream gravy with kasuri methi and tandoori-style charred chicken. Its origin is contested in court, so we do not pick a side.
Mexican component
Quesadilla con rajas: roasted poblano strips and Oaxaca-style cheese, griddled on a comal.
Fusion logic
The makhani is reduced until clingy so it stays inside, and poblano smoke and acid balance the richness. A dip is optional and served separately.
Texture target
Crisp-browned tortilla, set filling, melted cheese fused, no leak
Heat
low
Acid
poblano, optional lime, dip
Portion
One large folded tortilla, cut into wedges.
Plating
Wedges cut to show the cross-section, with the dip in a cup.
Cannot change without losing the dish
Chicken thigh, reduced makhani, roasted poblano rajas, Oaxaca-style cheese, tortilla, kasuri methi.
Beer idea
Vienna Amber (alternate: Hefeweizen)
Zero-proof idea
A lassi-inspired drink of cultured dairy, fruit and a little spice, served cold, to echo the sauce and cool the richness.
Operating risk
MEDIUM: steams soft if covered; filling leaks if sauce not reduced
Cultural care
Medium. The dish's origin is disputed, so we should tell no single origin story, and the quesadilla con rajas is borrowed from Mexican home cooking and should be credited.
Next test
Session 4: sauce thickness first (spoon-coat/reduction time vs leak minutes); then cheese barrier; then chicken size

Vegetarian story

Vegetarian is not a side.

Both India and Mexico have strong plant-based cooking traditions we want to learn from. NASHA designs vegetarian dishes as headliners, not substitutes.

Labels say “vegetarian as designed”. They are not a certified dietary statement; cross-contact is not assessed yet.

  • Chaat Elote — Charred corn with chile, lime and a crisp topping, intended to taste like street corn from two roadsides.
  • Dal-Frijol Dip — A slow-simmered black lentil and bean dip with a spiced-butter finish, for tearing bread and chips.
  • Gobi Taco — Crisp spiced cauliflower, tamarind-chile glaze and lime slaw in corn tortillas.
  • Paneer Tikka Taco — Charred yogurt-marinated paneer with green salsa and pineapple, intended to stay tender in a corn tortilla.
  • Toasted Seed & Chile Vegetable Bowl — Vegetables in a sauce of toasted nuts, seeds and dried chile, intended to be neither a mole nor a curry.
  • Cardamom Churros — Crisp churros dusted with cardamom sugar, with a dark jaggery-chocolate sauce.

Fire

Char, smoke, quick heat.

Tandoor-style heat and a hot comal give the food its edges. Fire is how the kitchen is designed to work, and how the beer is meant to be met.

“Fusion” means a dish we invented by combining two traditions. “Inspired by” means built from a tradition without claiming to be it. The lamb dish depends on an unresolved cut decision.

NASHA is a future Indo-Mex brewery and kitchen in Austin, Texas, in development.

The name was chosen by the founder. Legal clearance of the name is pending. Nothing here claims trademark ownership. There is no brewery, restaurant or truck open, and nothing is for sale. No site has been chosen.

In Hindi and Urdu, nasha means intoxication or addiction. We chose it for the feeling of being drawn in by food, craft and company. We take that meaning seriously and will never present excess or addiction as something to admire. Cultural advisors will review the name and our language before launch.

Images show a possible future. The photographic-style pictures are concept visualizations made with AI tools and edited, and the drawings are illustrations. They are not photographs of NASHA, of its food, or of its beer. About these images.

Menu items are designs for testing, not served food. Heat and vegetarian labels describe how a dish is designed, not a certified allergen or dietary statement. Ask before you eat if you have an allergy. If you drink, drink responsibly. Alcohol is for adults of legal drinking age.

The word NASHA in the header and in some pictures is a temporary typographic placeholder, set in a standard font. It is not a logo, not an official brand mark, and no trademark is claimed. No logo has been approved or released.
